children: PMET Resources' updated CV5 feasibility study estimates pre-tax NPV8% of CA$8.5B versus CA$2.5B in the 2025 study, and pre-tax IRR of 47.2% versus 19.9%. FID remains targeted for late 2027, subject to approvals and financing.
Pre-tax NPV CA$8.5B vs CA$2.5B in 2025 study
The study projects a substantial uplift in project value, although it depends on its commodity-price assumptions and remains pre-development.
Higher projected returns strengthen the project's investment case but are feasibility-study estimates, not realized results.
The 18% projected reduction improves modeled cost competitiveness; tantalum credits contribute to the lower figure.
Total development capital ~CA$1.9B before tax credits
The funding requirement is significant, and the company has not made a final investment decision.
FID targeted for late 2027, subject to approvals and funding
Permitting and financing remain key milestones before construction can proceed.

This is an updated feasibility-stage assessment of a pre-production lithium-tantalum project, revising the economics previously published in 2025. Permitting, detailed engineering and securing financing will need to progress before the targeted late-2027 FID.
Based on the original press release from PMET Resources Inc. distributed by PR Newswire.
